messages:
marco: FYI ran into a weird WSL/Windows crossover bug with the new redwoodctl installer. Installed on Ubuntu-WSL2, and the postinstall wrote a `redwoodctl.exe` shim into C:\Users\marco\AppData\Local\Redwood\bin which ends up earlier in PATH for WSL shells. When I run `redwoodctl login` from WSL it tries to spawn `cmd /c start` to open the Windows browser and fails with ENOENT. It then retries 3x which clutters my logs and leaves partial token files.

anya: Ugh. Can you paste the error and `redwoodctl version`? Also which distro and Windows build?

marco: `redwoodctl 0.18.1` on Ubuntu 22.04 WSL2, Win11 build 26000. Error: `ERROR: open browser failed: spawn cmd ENOENT` followed by `WARN: retrying interactive login (attempt 2/3)`. After the retries I got a half-populated `/home/marco/.redwood/auth_state.json` and local-serve later failed with 401s.

anya: Two issues: (1) installer dropping a Windows shim into a location WSL picks up, (2) interactive login spawn logic assuming cmd/start exist in PATH. For WSL the correct behavior is to either call `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command Start-Process` or prefer device flow automatically.

ops-bot: Note: some WSL distros map /mnt/c/Users to Windows paths so path normalization matters here. If redwoodctl resolves config using Windows shortnames it can create mismatched files between WSL and Windows user home.

marco: Workaround: I uninstalled, reinstalled using the `--no-shim` flag and added `/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` (Linux binary) to PATH so WSL uses the native binary. Then `redwoodctl login --device` worked and produced a clean token cache.

anya: Thanks for the repro. Action items I'll file: - detect WSL on installer and avoid writing Windows shims into locations exposed to WSL by default - make `redwoodctl login` detect missing spawn targets (cmd/start/xdg-open) and auto-fallback to device flow with a clear log message instead of noisy retries - ensure auth is atomic so partial auth_state.json isn't left on failure.

marco: That would be great. Also request: add a brief note in docs about `--no-shim`/`--symlink` and WSL best practices. Happy to test patches.

devex-bot: Filed DEVEX-7957: installer: avoid Windows shims in WSL-accessible paths; DEVEX-7958: login: auto-fallback to device flow when interactive open fails; linked to eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:
